## Why? {#why}

**Research question:** How fast do drivers respond to a take-over request on average, and how many measurements are missing?

Before you compare groups or fit models, you look at the data: What is in it, which values are missing, what does R say when something goes wrong? This lesson shows the building blocks that appear in every later lesson. It uses the driving simulator study `driving_sim`: 40 participants, 12 take-overs each, reaction time `rt_ms`.

## Concept {#concept}

R code consists of a few building blocks:

```{=html}
<figure class="rt-figure">
<svg viewBox="0 0 560 150" role="img" aria-labelledby="fig-wr-title fig-wr-desc" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <title id="fig-wr-title">Anatomy of a line of R code</title>
  <desc id="fig-wr-desc">The line mean_rt gets mean of driving_sim dollar rt_ms, na.rm equals TRUE. Labelled are: the object left of the assignment arrow, the function, a column of a table and an argument.</desc>
  <text x="20" y="80" class="rt-fig-code">mean_rt &lt;- mean(driving_sim$rt_ms, na.rm = TRUE)</text>
  <rect x="14" y="62" width="64" height="26" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box-accent" />
  <rect x="102" y="62" width="38" height="26" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box" />
  <rect x="141" y="62" width="140" height="26" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box" />
  <rect x="289" y="62" width="101" height="26" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box" />
  <text x="46" y="45" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label">object</text>
  <text x="121" y="45" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label">function</text>
  <text x="211" y="120" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label">table$column</text>
  <text x="339" y="120" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label">argument</text>
  <text x="90" y="120" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label rt-fig-muted">&lt;- stores</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Left of the arrow is the name, right of it the calculation. Arguments control how a function computes.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

- **Objects** store results: `mean_rt <- ...`. Without `<-` the result is only shown, not stored.
- **Functions** compute: `mean(x)`. Their **arguments** are listed in the help (`?mean`), with defaults such as `na.rm = FALSE`.
- **Vectors and tables:** a column is a vector (`driving_sim$rt_ms`); a table (data frame, tibble) is a list of columns of equal length.
- **Missing values** are called `NA` ("not available"). Computing with `NA` gives `NA` until you explicitly say otherwise.
- **Text in quotes, names without:** `condition == "visual"` compares the column `condition` with the text `"visual"`.
- **The pipe `|>`** passes the result on the left as the first argument to the right. Read it as "and then".

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## More: reading error messages

R messages are short but precise. The most common ones:

| Message | Usually means |
|---|---|
| `object 'x' not found` | Typo, missing quotes, or code not run yet |
| `could not find function "f"` | Package not loaded (`library(pkg)` or `pkg::f()`) |
| `unexpected symbol` / `unexpected ')'` | A bracket or comma is missing or one too many |
| `argument "x" is missing, with no default` | A required argument was left out |
| `Warning: NAs introduced by coercion` | Text could not be converted to numbers; check the values |

A **warning** does not stop the code but deserves a look. An **error** stops it.
:::

## Example {#example}

A first look at the data: columns, types and the first values. Click **Run Code**; you can change the code and run it again.

```{webr}
glimpse(driving_sim)
```

How many reaction times are missing? `is.na()` returns `TRUE` or `FALSE` for every value, `sum()` counts the `TRUE`s:

```{webr}
sum(is.na(driving_sim$rt_ms))
```

That is why the mean is `NA` at first; with `na.rm = TRUE` it uses the available values:

```{webr}
mean(driving_sim$rt_ms)
mean(driving_sim$rt_ms, na.rm = TRUE)
```

The same as a **dplyr** pipeline, per warning modality:

```{webr}
driving_sim |>
  summarise(mean_rt = mean(rt_ms, na.rm = TRUE), n_missing = sum(is.na(rt_ms)), .by = condition)
```

**How to report it:** The mean reaction time was 1004 ms; 12 of 480 measurements (2.5%) were missing due to sensor dropouts.

## Package comparison {#packages}

| Approach | Strength | When |
|---|---|---|
| Base R: `mean(driving_sim$rt_ms, na.rm = TRUE)` | Short, no packages, found everywhere in other people's code | Single statistics, quick checks |
| dplyr: `driving_sim |> summarise(...)` | Reads top to bottom, groups with `.by`, result is a table | **Recommended** for anything beyond a single value |
| `glimpse()` / `str()` / `summary()` | Overview of columns, types, missing values | Always right after reading data |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Run locally

In the browser everything is set up. Locally, this works best:

1. **Create a project:** in RStudio *File → New Project*, in Positron open a folder. The project folder is then the working directory, and paths like `"data/driving_sim.csv"` work on every computer.
2. **Quarto document instead of loose scripts:** *File → New File → Quarto Document*. Text, code and results stay together and can be rendered to HTML or Word.
3. **Install packages once, load them in every session:**

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "easystats"))
library(dplyr)
```
:::

## Cheat sheet {#cheatsheet}

```r
# Overview
glimpse(driving_sim)
summary(driving_sim$rt_ms)

# Count missing values and leave them out on purpose
sum(is.na(driving_sim$rt_ms))
mean_rt <- round(mean(driving_sim$rt_ms, na.rm = TRUE), 1)

# Compare text: column without, value with quotes
driving_sim |> filter(condition == "visual")

# Help
?quantile
```

- `<-` stores; without `<-` the result is only shown.
- `NA` is contagious: computing with `NA` gives `NA`. Count first, then choose `na.rm = TRUE` on purpose.
- Read the error message first: which name, which function, which line?
